text:
sara: Seeing intermittent 502s from redwood-inference-gpu-svc in eu-west-1 after the overnight GPU scale. Started ~02:10 UTC.
mateo: We did a burst scale: 40 -> 46 GPUs, then down to 38 around 02:25. Nodes got drained and re-provisioned. kube-proxy logs show endpoint cache churn.
kevin: Pulling endpoint slices now: `kubectl -n infra get endpointslice -l kubernetes.io/service-name=redwood-inference-gpu-svc -o wide`
kevin: Output shows multiple slices with old pod IPs that belong to nodes terminated minutes ago.
ops-bot: node/gpu-node-77 terminated (autoscaler). node/gpu-node-81 added.
nora: On gpu-node-79 I see iptables still routing to 10.12.3.45 (pod on drained node). conntrack has entries for that IP.
sara: If kube-proxy isn't reconciling endpoints fast enough, traffic will be DNAT'd to dead IPs. rolling-restart of kube-proxy on a node fixed traffic for pods on that node.
mateo: Restart helped locally. This smells like kube-proxy endpoint cache staleness across the fleet after fast node churn from the autoscaler.
kevin: Possible fixes: force rolling restart of kube-proxy daemonset (maxUnavailable=1), or tune kube-proxy sync flags. We can also throttle autoscaler to reduce churn.
nora: Quick mitigation: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy --timeout=5m` — did that with maxUnavailable=1 manually, got immediate improvement.
sara: Thanks. We should avoid full fleet restarts during peak. Mateo, can you tweak the cluster-autoscaler settings to increase scaleDownUnneededTime and reduce surge?
mateo: On it. Proposing `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and `--max-graceful-termination-sec=600` for smoother drains. Also bumping `--node-group-min-size` safety for eu-west GPU pool.
kevin: I'll open a PR to add a monitoring alert for EndpointSlice <-> kube-proxy sync lag and an automatic remediation runbook to restart kube-proxy rollingly.
sara: Also adding a note in the inference runbook: when scaling GPUs rapidly, watch for stale endpoints and check `kubectl get endpointslice` + `kubectl describe node <node>`
ops-bot: incident/2026-03-18-gpu-egress-service created and assigned to platform oncall.
nora: After the restarts and CA tuning traffic looks stable, no further 502s in the last 7m.
sara: Closing the thread if nothing else crops up. Please paste follow-up PR/alerts here.
kevin: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/compare/endpointsync-alerts
mateo: CA config change rolled in eu-west canary cluster.
sara: :thumbsup: great cleanup — we should include tests for endpoint churn in chaos suite.
